chunks: From him, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darradj, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both), who said:
The divorce of the young man is valid if he has reached the age of discernment (akil), and his testimony and his will are valid, even if he has not yet experienced seminal emission (ihtilam).

key_terms.عَقَلَ: Reached the age of discernment / maturity of mind
key_terms.يَحْتَلِمْ: Experiences seminal emission (physical sign of puberty)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between 'akil' and 'muhallim' in Shia Islamic family law regarding marriage and divorce?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that the legal capacity (ahliyyah) for a young male (ghulam) to execute a valid divorce, will, and testimony rests on reaching the age of discernment (bulugh al--aql), rather than solely on the physical sign of seminal emission (ihtilam). This distinction highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on mental maturity and rational understanding as the primary determinants for independent legal agency in personal status matters.
